content: The World Health Organization (WHO) has developed a guide titled The WHO Application of ICD-10 to Deaths During Pregnancy, Childbirth, and the Puerperium: ICD-MM. This guide is based on the 10th revision of the International Statistical Classification of Diseases and Related Health Problems (ICD-10) and its coding rules. It aims to standardize the identification, classification, and reporting of maternal deaths to improve the accuracy and consistency of maternal mortality data globally. The guide was created to address inconsistencies in the reporting and classification of maternal deaths, which can lead to underreporting and misclassification. Accurate data on maternal mortality is essential for achieving Millennium Development Goal 5a, which aims to reduce maternal mortality by 75%. The guide provides a framework for healthcare providers, death certifiers, and researchers to document and analyze maternal deaths systematically. The document outlines the principles for identifying direct and indirect maternal deaths, as well as late maternal deaths. Direct maternal deaths result from obstetric complications during pregnancy, childbirth, or the puerperium, including interventions, omissions, or incorrect treatments. Indirect maternal deaths are caused by pre-existing or pregnancy-related conditions that are aggravated by the physiological effects of pregnancy. Late maternal deaths occur more than 42 days but less than one year after the termination of pregnancy due to direct or indirect causes. The guide emphasizes the importance of complete and accurate death certification. It provides detailed instructions on how to document the sequence of events leading to death, starting with the immediate cause and tracing back to the underlying cause. The inclusion of a pregnancy checkbox on death certificates is recommended to help identify whether a woman was pregnant or recently pregnant at the time of death. This has been shown to reduce underreporting of maternal deaths. The WHO guide also introduces a grouping system for maternal deaths using existing ICD-10 codes. This system facilitates the aggregation of data into meaningful categories for epidemiological analysis and public health planning. The guide includes appendices and tables to assist in the consistent reporting of clinical conditions, identification of contributory factors, and classification of deaths as direct or indirect maternal deaths. The development of the guide involved a consultative process with experts in obstetrics, midwifery, epidemiology, and public health from both developed and developing countries. It was tested on maternal death databases from various countries and revised based on feedback from stakeholders. The guide is intended to be used alongside the three volumes of ICD-10 and is adaptable for use in different settings, including those with limited data on causes of death. By applying the ICD-MM framework, countries can improve the quality and comparability of maternal mortality statistics. This will enhance the interpretation of data, inform resource allocation, and support the development of programs to address maternal mortality. The guide also highlights the need for future updates to incorporate new codes and details as they become available in ICD-11. In summary, the WHO Application of ICD-10 to Deaths During Pregnancy, Childbirth, and the Puerperium (ICD-MM) is a critical tool for improving the documentation, classification, and analysis of maternal deaths. It provides a standardized approach to understanding the causes and magnitude of maternal mortality, ultimately contributing to better public health outcomes for women worldwide.
